    Why should I join Arka Academy?

    Six Pillars. One Method. Six reasons to choose Arka.

    The six pillars in our emblem are not slogans. Each one is something we do for you, every day of your preparation.

    Pillar 01Endurance

    UPSC is decided by thousands of ordinary days, not one brilliant one.

    Preparation that runs every day

    Daily targets, tracked by your mentor, so your preparation never runs in bursts.

    Read the pillar

    UPSC is rarely decided on one brilliant day. It is decided by thousands of ordinary ones. Endurance is the quiet choice to return to the desk when enthusiasm has faded, and to keep a promise made to yourself long after the excitement of beginning is gone.

    Pillar 02Evaluation

    What is never measured is only imagined.

    Every answer evaluated, one by one

    Individual evaluation of your answers and tests, with specific written feedback and model answers.

    Read the pillar

    What is never measured is only imagined. Honest evaluation holds a mirror to your preparation, and the courage to look into it without excuse is what separates hope from progress.

    Pillar 03Execution

    A plan is only a wish until it is lived.

    A plan you actually live

    Your daily responsibility map turns the syllabus into tasks you complete, and we check that you did.

    Read the pillar

    A plan is only a wish until it is lived. Execution is the bridge between knowing and doing, where intention becomes hours, hours become habit and habit becomes result.

    Pillar 04Expression

    Understanding that cannot be written remains private.

    Answers that speak to the examiner

    Regular answer-writing and essay practice, so your thinking reaches the paper clearly.

    Read the pillar

    Understanding that cannot be spoken or written remains private. To express is to give thought a shape, so that a mind can speak clearly to an examiner and, in time, to the nation it hopes to serve.

    Pillar 05Equanimity

    A calm mind learns faster and judges better.

    A mentor beside you, one on one

    The teachers who teach you also mentor you, adjusting your strategy and keeping you steady through setbacks.

    Read the pillar

    The examination will test your composure as surely as your knowledge. Equanimity is the steadiness to meet uncertainty, setbacks and silence with a clear head, because a calm mind learns faster and judges better.

    Pillar 06Ethics

    Before a candidate becomes an officer, they must become a person worth trusting.

    Honest from the first day

    We never borrow anyone’s results. Judge us free first, through our free classes and a free one-hour demo.

    Read the pillar

    Before a candidate becomes an officer, they must become a person worth trusting. Ethics is the discipline of choosing what is right even when it is inconvenient, the one preparation that continues long after the results.

    Practice. Evaluate. Improve. Repeat.

    About Arka Academy

    An Institution Built Around the Realities of Preparation.

    Arka Academy, founded by Mr. Rishi Singh Rajput, is an academic initiative dedicated to making UPSC Civil Services preparation more structured, accountable and purposeful.

    We began in August 2026 with one question: what is actually missing in the way most aspirants prepare? This page explains what we found, what we believe, and how we have built Arka around it.

    Book a free demoRead the founder’s message
    Who we areOur name and emblemOur beliefOur purposeOur approachFounder’s message

    Who we are

    Information is only the starting point. Execution is the real challenge.

    We exist to turn what an aspirant knows into what an aspirant does, day after day, until the examination.

    We recognise that understanding the syllabus, identifying the right books and knowing the examination pattern are only the starting points of preparation. The real challenge lies in translating this understanding into consistent action.

    Completing targets, maintaining discipline, revising effectively, practising regularly, identifying weaknesses and improving performance over an extended period require much more than information or occasional guidance. They require a well-defined academic approach.

    At Arka Academy, we strive to create an environment where learning is systematic, preparation is purposeful and academic progress is continuously pursued.

    Our promise

    Each day, what you must do and what your mentor must do is written down and checked off, on both sides. And we do not step away when a course ends: we stay beside you until you have sat for at least one UPSC Mains.

    Our name and emblem

    Why “Arka”?

    Arka (अर्क) is the Sanskrit word for the sun, the one presence that never misses a day. That is the kind of preparation we want for every aspirant: steady, daily and dependable, whatever the weather.

    Our emblem is a gateway held up by six carved stone pillars: the way into a life of public service. Each pillar carries one principle of preparation: Endurance, Evaluation, Execution, Expression, Equanimity and Ethics. Together they form the Arka Method.

    Explore the six pillars

    Our belief

    Knowing How to Prepare Is Not Enough. What Matters Is How Consistently You Execute.

    The Civil Services Examination demands knowledge, analytical ability and effective articulation. But the journey towards it demands discipline, patience, resilience and sustained effort.

    An aspirant may have access to the best books, resources and guidance, yet struggle to maintain consistency or translate preparation into performance. Effective preparation is not simply about accumulating information or completing the syllabus. It is about understanding concepts, applying knowledge, practising regularly and continuously refining one’s approach.

    Preparation becomes meaningful when learning translates into action, and action leads to improvement.

    Our purpose

    To Make Preparation More Structured, Purposeful and Effective.

    What aspirants usually have

    An enormous amount of information, study material, lectures and test series. Access to resources is rarely the problem.

    What they usually lack

    A way to organise, prioritise and execute all of it, day after day, with someone checking the work and telling them the truth about it.

    Arka Academy seeks to close this gap. Our purpose is to provide an academic environment where:

    01Learning is aligned with the actual demands of the examination.
    02Concepts are developed through systematic teaching.
    03Preparation is organised around the UPSC syllabus.
    04Practice and revision become integral to learning.
    05Evaluation helps identify areas requiring improvement.
    06Academic guidance remains focused on individual progress.

    Our educational approach

    Learning with Direction. Preparing with Purpose.

    Every stage of preparation at Arka has a clear academic objective. Each one feeds the next, and the cycle repeats until the examination.

    1. Conceptual learning
    2. Syllabus-oriented preparation
    3. PYQ analysis
    4. Current affairs integration
    5. Answer-writing practice
    6. Evaluation
    7. Revision

    Understanding

    over rote memorisation

    Application

    over information accumulation

    Improvement

    over the mere completion of targets

    Our courses build the knowledge, analytical ability, articulation and examination temperament the Civil Services Examination demands, guided by six pillars and a shared commitment to accountability between mentors and aspirants.

    The vision behind Arka

    A message from our founder

    “

    Dear aspirant,

    Over the years, I have watched many capable aspirants lose their way in this examination. Rarely for lack of intelligence, and rarely for lack of books or lectures. Far more often, it was because nobody held their preparation together. Nobody checked whether the day’s work was actually done. Nobody told them honestly where their answers fell short. And nobody stayed when the results did not come.

    Arka Academy was started to fill exactly that gap.

    Here, preparation is not left to motivation. Every day, your responsibilities and ours are set out and tracked. Every answer you write is read and evaluated. And we do not walk away when a course ends: we stay with you until you have written at least one UPSC Mains.

    I cannot promise you that this journey will be easy. I can promise that you will not walk it alone, and that we will hold ourselves to the same discipline we ask of you.

    Come and sit in a class first. Judge us by how we teach, not by what we claim.

    Rishi Singh RajputFounder, Arka Academy

    Inside Arka

    Every topic, taught, tested and improved before we move on.

    At Arka, a topic is not “done” when the lecture ends. It is done when you have understood it, explained it to your mentor, tested yourself on it, written about it, and been shown how to write it better. Here is exactly how that happens.

    Book a free demoSee the learning cycle
    Learning cycleTestsRevisionWith every topicIf you fall behindA week at ArkaStudent voicesPolicies

    How every topic works

    One topic. Eight steps. No shortcuts.

    Each step has an owner: your teacher, your mentor or you. Each is marked on your daily responsibility map, so nothing is skipped and nothing is forgotten.

    1. 1

      We teach you

      Teacher

      Every topic begins with a live class. Your teacher builds the concept from the basics, connects it to the UPSC syllabus and previous year questions, and shows you how it is asked in the examination.

      Class delivered, marked by your teacher
    2. 2

      Notes in your hands

      Teacher

      After the class you receive structured notes for the topic. Everything you need to revise is in one place, so your time goes into understanding rather than searching.

      Notes shared
    3. 3

      You build your understanding

      You

      Read the notes, revisit the class and make the topic your own. Stuck anywhere? Call your mentor. Doubts are cleared one on one, not left for later. When you are confident, you tick “Understood”.

      You tick “Understood”
    4. 4

      The mentor’s call: an oral test

      Mentor

      Once you tick “Understood”, your mentor calls you and asks questions on the topic, just like an interview. Can you explain it in your own words? Can you connect it to current events? It shows what you really know and builds confidence for the personality test.

      Oral test done, marked by your mentor
    5. 5

      Test yourself, the Prelims way

      You

      You take an MCQ test on the topic, set in the UPSC Prelims pattern, so you practise accuracy and elimination on what you have just learnt.

      MCQ test attempted
    6. 6

      Write it, the Mains way

      You

      You receive Mains questions on the same topic and write your answers within the time limit, turning understanding into expression.

      Answers submitted
    7. 7

      Evaluation and discussion

      Teacher + mentor

      Your answers are evaluated individually, with written feedback and model answers. The MCQ test is discussed in detail: why each option is right or wrong, and how to eliminate.

      Evaluated and discussed
    8. 8

      The improvement call

      Mentor

      After evaluation your mentor calls you again. Together you go through your answers: what worked, what was missing, and exactly how to write better next time.

      Improvement call done
    9. Then, and only then, we move to the next topic.

    Checking progress

    Small tests every week. A bigger picture every month.

    Every week

    Weekly test

    Covers the topics of the week, in both MCQ and answer-writing format. It shows whether this week’s learning has stayed with you.

    Every month

    Monthly test

    Brings together everything covered so far. It measures your improvement over time, not just your score on one day.

    Always on record

    Your progress, tracked

    Every result is recorded, so you and your mentor can see your growth month by month and decide where to focus next.

    Month 1Month 2Month 3Month 4

    Revision

    What you learn in January should still be with you in May.

    Revision classes

    Planned at regular intervals alongside new topics, so earlier topics are never forgotten while you move ahead.

    Revision module

    A compact module for quick, focused revision of everything you have covered.

    Revision schedule

    A clear calendar telling you what to revise and when, built around your test dates.

    For every single topic, you receive:

    • A live class, with the recording
    • Structured notes
    • One-on-one doubt support from your mentor
    • An oral test call with your mentor
    • A Prelims MCQ test, with discussion
    • Mains answer-writing questions

    Life happens

    Missed a day? We notice, and we help you catch up.

    Illness, family responsibilities or a difficult week can happen to anyone. When your responsibility map shows missed tasks, your mentor reaches out, not to scold you, but to plan your catch-up with you.

    What firstThe tasks that matter most this week

    The only prerequisiteएकमात्र शर्त

    We teach everything from scratch, so you need no prior background. The one thing you must bring is the courage to fulfil your daily responsibilities, every single day. Bring that, and we bring the system, the teaching and the accountability that turn effort into results.

    हम सब कुछ शुरुआत से पढ़ाते हैं, इसलिए किसी पूर्व ज्ञान की ज़रूरत नहीं है। आपको बस एक चीज़ लानी है: हर दिन अपनी दैनिक ज़िम्मेदारियाँ पूरी करने का साहस। आप वह लाइए, और हम वह व्यवस्था, शिक्षण और जवाबदेही लाएँगे जो मेहनत को परिणाम में बदलती है।

    Who it is forयह किसके लिए है

    • Beginners starting UPSC preparation from zero
    • Graduates and final-year students who want one complete path, not scattered courses
    • Aspirants who have studied before but never had a system that held them to it
    • शून्य से UPSC की तैयारी शुरू करने वाले
    • स्नातक और अंतिम वर्ष के छात्र, जो अलग-अलग कोर्स की जगह एक पूरा रास्ता चाहते हैं
    • वे अभ्यर्थी जो पहले पढ़ चुके हैं, पर उन्हें कभी ऐसी व्यवस्था नहीं मिली जो उन्हें नियमित रखे

    What you getआपको क्या मिलेगा

    • Complete coverage of Prelims GS Paper I, Prelims CSAT (Paper II), Essay and Mains GS Papers I–IV
    • Live classes with recordings, and structured notes for every topic
    • The full 8-step Arka learning cycle on every topic
    • Weekly and monthly tests, revision classes, a revision module and a revision schedule
    • A daily responsibility map, tracked by you and your mentor
    • Mentorship that continues until you have written at least one Mains
    • प्रीलिम्स GS पेपर I, प्रीलिम्स CSAT (पेपर II), निबंध और मेन्स GS पेपर I–IV की पूरी तैयारी
    • रिकॉर्डिंग के साथ लाइव कक्षाएँ, और हर टॉपिक के व्यवस्थित नोट्स
    • हर टॉपिक पर अर्क लर्निंग साइकिल के पूरे 8 चरण
    • साप्ताहिक और मासिक टेस्ट, रिवीज़न कक्षाएँ, रिवीज़न मॉड्यूल और रिवीज़न शेड्यूल
    • दैनिक ज़िम्मेदारी मैप, जिसे आप और आपके मेंटर दोनों ट्रैक करते हैं
    • मेंटरशिप जो तब तक चलती है जब तक आप कम से कम एक मेन्स नहीं लिख लेते

    The optional subject is not part of this programme. It has its own batch: see Public Administration Optional.वैकल्पिक विषय इस प्रोग्राम का हिस्सा नहीं है। उसका अलग बैच है: लोक प्रशासन वैकल्पिक देखें।

    How every topic worksहर टॉपिक कैसे चलता है

    1. We teach you in a live class.
    2. You receive structured notes.
    3. You build your understanding; doubts go to your mentor on call. You tick “Understood”.
    4. Your mentor calls you for an oral, interview-style test on the topic.
    5. You take a Prelims MCQ test on the topic.
    6. You write Mains answers on the topic.
    7. Your answers are evaluated and the MCQs discussed.
    8. Your mentor calls you to explain how to improve. Then we move to the next topic.
    1. हम लाइव कक्षा में पढ़ाते हैं।
    2. आपको व्यवस्थित नोट्स मिलते हैं।
    3. आप अपनी समझ बनाते हैं; कोई भी संदेह हो तो मेंटर को कॉल करें। फिर आप “समझ लिया” पर टिक करते हैं।
    4. मेंटर आपको कॉल करके टॉपिक पर इंटरव्यू जैसा मौखिक टेस्ट लेते हैं।
    5. आप टॉपिक पर प्रीलिम्स MCQ टेस्ट देते हैं।
    6. आप टॉपिक पर मेन्स उत्तर लिखते हैं।
    7. आपके उत्तरों का मूल्यांकन होता है और MCQ पर चर्चा होती है।
    8. मेंटर कॉल करके बताते हैं कि सुधार कैसे करें। इसके बाद ही हम अगले टॉपिक पर जाते हैं।

    मेन्स GS IIसंविधान और राजव्यवस्था, शासन, सामाजिक न्याय, अंतरराष्ट्रीय संबंध

    मेन्स GS IVनीतिशास्त्र, सत्यनिष्ठा और अभिरुचि, केस स्टडी के साथ

    The ideaमूल विचार

    Prelims is not lost for lack of books. It is lost to scattered days, unrevised notes and nerves in the exam hall. In the Crucible, every hour of your day has a purpose, and your mentor tracks every one of them. You fight the battle; we show you where to aim.

    प्रीलिम्स किताबों की कमी से नहीं छूटता। यह बिखरे हुए दिनों, बिना रिवीज़न के नोट्स और परीक्षा हॉल की घबराहट से छूटता है। क्रूसिबल में आपके दिन का हर घंटा किसी उद्देश्य से जुड़ा है, और आपके मेंटर हर घंटे को ट्रैक करते हैं। युद्ध आप लड़ते हैं; लक्ष्य हम दिखाते हैं।

    Who it is forयह किसके लिए है

    • Aspirants appearing for UPSC Prelims 2027
    • Those who have studied the syllabus but need daily practice, tests and revision
    • UPSC प्रीलिम्स 2027 देने वाले अभ्यर्थी
    • वे जिन्होंने सिलेबस पढ़ा है, पर जिन्हें रोज़ का अभ्यास, टेस्ट और रिवीज़न चाहिए

    What you getआपको क्या मिलेगा

    • 1.5 years of current affairs, covered in daily morning classes
    • A daily CSAT class: concept, PYQs and practice MCQs
    • A daily target with detailed notes for the topic of the day
    • Morning and evening MCQ practice, every day
    • A nightly class on the last 20 years’ PYQs, discussed in detail
    • 60 Prelims tests: 40 sectional and 20 full-length
    • 10 CSAT tests
    • 5 complete revisions, with a personal revision schedule
    • Exam-hall mindset sessions, so you walk in calm and walk out confident
    • Daily tracking on your responsibility map, as promised
    • रोज़ सुबह की कक्षाओं में 1.5 वर्ष की समसामयिकी
    • रोज़ CSAT कक्षा: अवधारणा, PYQ और अभ्यास MCQ
    • दिन के टॉपिक के विस्तृत नोट्स के साथ दैनिक लक्ष्य
    • हर दिन सुबह और शाम MCQ अभ्यास
    • पिछले 20 वर्षों के PYQ पर रोज़ रात की कक्षा, विस्तार से चर्चा
    • 60 प्रीलिम्स टेस्ट: 40 सेक्शनल और 20 फुल-लेंथ
    • 10 CSAT टेस्ट
    • व्यक्तिगत रिवीज़न शेड्यूल के साथ 5 पूरे रिवीज़न
    • परीक्षा हॉल की मानसिकता पर सत्र, ताकि आप शांत मन से जाएँ और आत्मविश्वास से लौटें
    • वादे के अनुसार आपके ज़िम्मेदारी मैप पर रोज़ की ट्रैकिंग

    Syllabus coveredकवर किया गया सिलेबस

    Prelims GS Paper I (current events, history and the national movement, geography, polity and governance, economic and social development, environment and ecology, general science) and CSAT Paper II (comprehension, reasoning, decision making, mental ability, basic numeracy, data interpretation).

    प्रीलिम्स GS पेपर I (समसामयिक घटनाएँ, इतिहास और राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन, भूगोल, राजव्यवस्था और शासन, आर्थिक और सामाजिक विकास, पर्यावरण और पारिस्थितिकी, सामान्य विज्ञान) और CSAT पेपर II (बोधगम्यता, तर्कशक्ति, निर्णय लेना, मानसिक योग्यता, मूल गणित, डेटा व्याख्या)।

    Who it is forयह किसके लिए है

    • Aspirants who have studied the syllabus but struggle to turn knowledge into scoring answers
    • Those preparing for their first Mains, or improving after an earlier attempt
    • वे अभ्यर्थी जिन्होंने सिलेबस पढ़ा है, पर ज्ञान को अंक दिलाने वाले उत्तरों में नहीं बदल पाते
    • पहले मेन्स की तैयारी करने वाले, या पिछले प्रयास के बाद सुधार चाहने वाले

    What you getआपको क्या मिलेगा

    • 800 PYQs, topic by topic, across GS Papers I, II, III and IV
    • Daily evaluation of every answer you submit, with model answers
    • A detailed feedback call within 24 hours of your submission
    • A 3-hour test at the end of each GS paper, followed by a year-by-year discussion of the last 8 years’ PYQs of that paper
    • A full UPSC-style mock over two days: GS I, II, III and IV, in an exam-hall setting at a school, just as UPSC conducts it
    • Notes for each subject, and later short notes for fast revision
    • Daily tracking on your responsibility map
    • GS पेपर I, II, III और IV के 800 PYQ, टॉपिक के अनुसार
    • आपके हर उत्तर का दैनिक मूल्यांकन, मॉडल उत्तरों के साथ
    • उत्तर जमा करने के 24 घंटे के भीतर कॉल पर विस्तृत फीडबैक
    • हर GS पेपर के अंत में 3 घंटे का टेस्ट, उसके बाद उस पेपर के पिछले 8 वर्षों के PYQ पर वर्ष-वार चर्चा
    • दो दिन का पूरा UPSC-शैली मॉक: GS I, II, III और IV, किसी स्कूल में परीक्षा हॉल जैसे माहौल में, ठीक वैसे ही जैसे UPSC कराता है
    • हर विषय के नोट्स, और बाद में तेज़ रिवीज़न के लिए शॉर्ट नोट्स
    • आपके ज़िम्मेदारी मैप पर रोज़ की ट्रैकिंग

    How it worksयह कैसे चलता है

    1. You receive the day’s PYQs for the current topic.
    2. You write and submit your answers within the time limit.
    3. Your answers are evaluated the same day, with a model answer.
    4. Within 24 hours of submission, your mentor calls you with detailed feedback.
    5. You improve your answer and move to the next set.
    6. At the end of each paper: a 3-hour test, then the 8-year PYQ discussion.
    1. आपको चल रहे टॉपिक के उस दिन के PYQ मिलते हैं।
    2. आप समय-सीमा में उत्तर लिखकर जमा करते हैं।
    3. उसी दिन आपके उत्तरों का मूल्यांकन होता है, मॉडल उत्तर के साथ।
    4. जमा करने के 24 घंटे के भीतर मेंटर कॉल पर विस्तृत फीडबैक देते हैं।
    5. आप अपना उत्तर सुधारते हैं और अगले सेट पर जाते हैं।
    6. हर पेपर के अंत में: 3 घंटे का टेस्ट, फिर 8 वर्षों के PYQ पर चर्चा।

    GS I (विरासत और संस्कृति, इतिहास, समाज, भूगोल) · GS II (राजव्यवस्था, शासन, सामाजिक न्याय, अंतरराष्ट्रीय संबंध) · GS III (अर्थव्यवस्था, कृषि, इन्फ्रास्ट्रक्चर, विज्ञान और प्रौद्योगिकी, पर्यावरण, आपदा प्रबंधन, आंतरिक सुरक्षा) · GS IV (नीतिशास्त्र, सत्यनिष्ठा, अभिरुचि, केस स्टडी)

    Syllabus coveredकवर किया गया सिलेबस

    • Ethics and human interface: essence, determinants and consequences of ethics in human actions; ethics in private and public relationships; human values and lessons from leaders, reformers and administrators; the role of family, society and education
    • Attitude: content, structure and function; moral and political attitudes; social influence and persuasion
    • Aptitude and foundational values for civil service: integrity, impartiality, non-partisanship, objectivity, dedication to public service, empathy, tolerance and compassion
    • Emotional intelligence: concepts and their use in administration and governance
    • Moral thinkers and philosophers from India and the world
    • Public service values and ethics in public administration: ethical dilemmas, laws and conscience as guides, accountability, ethics in international relations and funding, corporate governance
    • Probity in governance: public service, transparency and the right to information, codes of ethics and conduct, citizen’s charters, work culture, service delivery, use of public funds, corruption
    • Case studies on all of the above
    • नीतिशास्त्र और मानवीय संबंध: मानवीय कार्यों में नैतिकता का सार, निर्धारक और परिणाम; निजी और सार्वजनिक संबंधों में नैतिकता; मानवीय मूल्य और नेताओं, सुधारकों व प्रशासकों से सीख; परिवार, समाज और शिक्षा की भूमिका
    • अभिवृत्ति: विषय-वस्तु, संरचना और कार्य; नैतिक और राजनीतिक अभिवृत्ति; सामाजिक प्रभाव और अनुनय
    • सिविल सेवा के लिए अभिरुचि और मूलभूत मूल्य: सत्यनिष्ठा, निष्पक्षता, गैर-दलगतता, वस्तुनिष्ठता, लोक सेवा के प्रति समर्पण, सहानुभूति, सहिष्णुता और करुणा
    • भावनात्मक बुद्धिमत्ता: अवधारणाएँ और प्रशासन व शासन में उनका उपयोग
    • भारत और विश्व के नैतिक चिंतक और दार्शनिक
    • लोक सेवा मूल्य और लोक प्रशासन में नैतिकता: नैतिक दुविधाएँ, कानून और अंतरात्मा मार्गदर्शक के रूप में, जवाबदेही, अंतरराष्ट्रीय संबंधों और वित्तपोषण में नैतिकता, कॉर्पोरेट शासन
    • शासन में ईमानदारी: लोक सेवा, पारदर्शिता और सूचना का अधिकार, आचार संहिता और नीति संहिता, नागरिक चार्टर, कार्य संस्कृति, सेवा वितरण, सार्वजनिक धन का उपयोग, भ्रष्टाचार
    • उपरोक्त सभी विषयों पर केस स्टडी

    Who it is forयह किसके लिए है

    • Aspirants who find it hard to start, structure or balance an essay
    • Those who want their 250-mark Essay paper to stop being a gamble
    • वे अभ्यर्थी जिन्हें निबंध शुरू करने, उसकी संरचना बनाने या संतुलन रखने में कठिनाई होती है
    • वे जो चाहते हैं कि 250 अंकों का निबंध पेपर अब अनिश्चित न रहे

    What you getआपको क्या मिलेगा

    • 10 essays over 3 months, one about every 9 days
    • A class on each theme: how to read the topic, find dimensions and build an argument
    • The Arka cycle for every essay, as in the Foundation Programme
    • Individual evaluation of every essay, with detailed written feedback
    • An improvement call after every evaluation
    • Daily tracking on your responsibility map
    • 3 महीनों में 10 निबंध, लगभग हर 9 दिन में एक
    • हर विषय पर कक्षा: टॉपिक कैसे समझें, आयाम कैसे खोजें, तर्क कैसे गढ़ें
    • फाउंडेशन प्रोग्राम की तरह हर निबंध के लिए अर्क साइकिल
    • हर निबंध का व्यक्तिगत मूल्यांकन, विस्तृत लिखित फीडबैक के साथ
    • हर मूल्यांकन के बाद सुधार कॉल
    • आपके ज़िम्मेदारी मैप पर रोज़ की ट्रैकिंग

    How every essay worksहर निबंध कैसे चलता है

    1. Theme class: reading the topic, brainstorming dimensions, structuring the argument.
    2. Your outline: you prepare the outline and tick “Ready”.
    3. Mentor’s call: your mentor discusses your outline with you before you write.
    4. You write: the full essay, within the exam time limit.
    5. Evaluation: structure, depth, balance, examples and language, with written feedback.
    6. Improvement call: what worked, what was missing, how the next essay will be better.
    1. विषय कक्षा: टॉपिक को समझना, आयामों पर विचार करना, तर्क की संरचना बनाना।
    2. आपकी रूपरेखा: आप रूपरेखा तैयार करते हैं और “तैयार” पर टिक करते हैं।
    3. मेंटर की कॉल: लिखने से पहले मेंटर आपके साथ रूपरेखा पर चर्चा करते हैं।
    4. आप लिखते हैं: परीक्षा की समय-सीमा में पूरा निबंध।
    5. मूल्यांकन: संरचना, गहराई, संतुलन, उदाहरण और भाषा, लिखित फीडबैक के साथ।
    6. सुधार कॉल: क्या अच्छा रहा, क्या छूटा, और अगला निबंध बेहतर कैसे होगा।

    UPSC syllabus

    The syllabus below follows the Civil Services Examination notification issued by UPSC. Read it with the latest notification on upsc.gov.in, which is the final authority.

    Prelims: Paper I, General Studies (200 marks, 2 hours)
    • Current events of national and international importance.
    • History of India and the Indian National Movement.
    • Indian and world geography: physical, social and economic geography of India and the world.
    • Indian polity and governance: Constitution, political system, Panchayati Raj, public policy, rights issues and so on.
    • Economic and social development: sustainable development, poverty, inclusion, demographics, social sector initiatives and so on.
    • General issues on environmental ecology, biodiversity and climate change that do not require subject specialisation.
    • General science.
    Prelims: Paper II, CSAT (200 marks, 2 hours, qualifying at 33%)
    • Comprehension.
    • Interpersonal skills including communication skills.
    • Logical reasoning and analytical ability.
    • Decision making and problem solving.
    • General mental ability.
    • Basic numeracy (numbers and their relations, orders of magnitude and so on) and data interpretation (charts, graphs, tables, data sufficiency), Class X level.
    • English language comprehension skills, Class X level.
    Mains: Essay (250 marks)

    Candidates may be required to write essays on multiple topics. They are expected to keep closely to the subject, arrange their ideas in an orderly fashion and write concisely. Credit is given for effective and exact expression. The paper currently has two sections, and you write one essay from each.

    Mains: General Studies I, Heritage, History, Geography and Society
    • Indian culture: salient aspects of art forms, literature and architecture from ancient to modern times.
    • Modern Indian history from about the middle of the eighteenth century until the present: significant events, personalities and issues.
    • The freedom struggle: its various stages and important contributors from different parts of the country.
    • Post-independence consolidation and reorganisation within the country.
    • History of the world: events from the 18th century such as the industrial revolution, world wars, redrawing of national boundaries, colonisation, decolonisation, and political philosophies like communism, capitalism and socialism, with their forms and effects on society.
    • Salient features of Indian society and the diversity of India.
    • Role of women and women’s organisations; population and associated issues; poverty and developmental issues; urbanisation, problems and remedies.
    • Effects of globalisation on Indian society.
    • Social empowerment, communalism, regionalism and secularism.
    • Salient features of the world’s physical geography.
    • Distribution of key natural resources across the world (including South Asia and the Indian subcontinent); factors responsible for the location of primary, secondary and tertiary sector industries in various parts of the world (including India).
    • Important geophysical phenomena such as earthquakes, tsunami, volcanic activity and cyclones; geographical features and their location; changes in critical geographical features (including water bodies and ice-caps) and in flora and fauna, and the effects of such changes.
    Mains: General Studies II, Governance, Constitution, Polity, Social Justice and International Relations
    • Indian Constitution: historical underpinnings, evolution, features, amendments, significant provisions and basic structure.
    • Functions and responsibilities of the Union and the States; issues and challenges of the federal structure; devolution of powers and finances up to local levels.
    • Separation of powers between organs; dispute redressal mechanisms and institutions.
    • Comparison of the Indian constitutional scheme with that of other countries.
    • Parliament and State legislatures: structure, functioning, conduct of business, powers and privileges, and issues arising out of these.
    • Structure, organisation and functioning of the Executive and the Judiciary; Ministries and Departments; pressure groups and formal and informal associations and their role in the polity.
    • Salient features of the Representation of the People Act.
    • Appointment to various constitutional posts; powers, functions and responsibilities of constitutional bodies; statutory, regulatory and quasi-judicial bodies.
    • Government policies and interventions for development in various sectors, and issues arising from their design and implementation.
    • Development processes and the development industry: role of NGOs, SHGs, associations, donors, charities and other stakeholders.
    • Welfare schemes for vulnerable sections by the Centre and States and their performance; mechanisms, laws, institutions and bodies for their protection and betterment.
    • Issues relating to development and management of social sector and services: health, education, human resources.
    • Issues relating to poverty and hunger.
    • Governance, transparency and accountability; e-governance applications, models, successes, limitations and potential; citizens’ charters and institutional measures.
    • Role of civil services in a democracy.
    • India and its neighbourhood: relations.
    • Bilateral, regional and global groupings and agreements involving India or affecting India’s interests.
    • Effect of policies and politics of developed and developing countries on India’s interests; Indian diaspora.
    • Important international institutions, agencies and fora: their structure and mandate.
    Mains: General Studies III, Technology, Economic Development, Biodiversity, Environment, Security and Disaster Management
    • Indian economy and issues relating to planning, mobilisation of resources, growth, development and employment.
    • Inclusive growth and issues arising from it.
    • Government budgeting.
    • Major crops and cropping patterns; types of irrigation and irrigation systems; storage, transport and marketing of agricultural produce and related constraints; e-technology in aid of farmers.
    • Direct and indirect farm subsidies and minimum support prices; Public Distribution System: objectives, functioning, limitations, revamping; buffer stocks and food security; technology missions; economics of animal rearing.
    • Food processing and related industries: scope, significance, location, upstream and downstream requirements, supply chain management.
    • Land reforms in India.
    • Effects of liberalisation on the economy; changes in industrial policy and their effects on industrial growth.
    • Infrastructure: energy, ports, roads, airports, railways and so on; investment models.
    • Science and technology: developments, applications and effects in everyday life; achievements of Indians; indigenisation of technology and development of new technology.
    • Awareness in IT, space, computers, robotics, nanotechnology and biotechnology; issues relating to intellectual property rights.
    • Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment.
    • Disaster and disaster management.
    • Linkages between development and spread of extremism.
    • Role of external state and non-state actors in creating challenges to internal security.
    • Challenges to internal security through communication networks; role of media and social networking sites; basics of cyber security; money laundering and its prevention.
    • Security challenges and their management in border areas; linkages of organised crime with terrorism.
    • Various security forces and agencies and their mandate.
    Mains: General Studies IV, Ethics, Integrity and Aptitude
    • Ethics and human interface: essence, determinants and consequences of ethics in human action; dimensions of ethics; ethics in private and public relationships.
    • Human values: lessons from the lives and teachings of great leaders, reformers and administrators; role of family, society and educational institutions in inculcating values.
    • Attitude: content, structure, function; its influence on and relation with thought and behaviour; moral and political attitudes; social influence and persuasion.
    • Aptitude and foundational values for civil service: integrity, impartiality and non-partisanship, objectivity, dedication to public service, empathy, tolerance and compassion towards weaker sections.
    • Emotional intelligence: concepts, utility and application in administration and governance.
    • Contributions of moral thinkers and philosophers from India and the world.
    • Public and civil service values and ethics in public administration: status and problems; ethical concerns and dilemmas in government and private institutions; laws, rules, regulations and conscience as sources of ethical guidance; accountability and ethical governance; strengthening moral values in governance; ethical issues in international relations and funding; corporate governance.
    • Probity in governance: concept of public service; philosophical basis of governance and probity; information sharing and transparency; Right to Information; codes of ethics and conduct; citizens’ charters; work culture; quality of service delivery; utilisation of public funds; challenges of corruption.
    • Case studies on the above issues.
    Mains: Qualifying language papers

    Paper A (Indian language) and Paper B (English), 300 marks each. They test comprehension, précis writing, usage and vocabulary, short essays and translation. You need the qualifying marks in the notification, and these marks are not counted in the merit ranking.

    Optional subject

    Two papers of 250 marks each, in a subject you choose from the list in the notification. Public Administration is taught at Arka, see the course page.

    Interview (Personality Test), 275 marks

    A conversation with a board that judges your suitability for a career in public service: mental alertness, critical thinking, balance of judgement, clarity and honesty of expression, and ethical grounding.

    Marks counted for merit: 1750 (Mains) + 275 (Interview) = 2025.

    Preparation and strategy

    What the pattern of recent papers suggests, and how we advise students to prepare.

    Prelims strategy

    • GS Paper I is 200 marks with one-third negative marking. Accuracy matters more than attempts.
    • Build the base with NCERTs, then one standard book per subject. Do not add sources endlessly.
    • Use previous-year papers to learn how UPSC frames options, then revise at least twice.
    • Link each current-affairs item to its static topic, since many questions mix the two.
    • Take a test every week. Review why wrong options tempted you and fix that habit.
    • CSAT is qualifying at 33%. Practise it regularly so it never costs you the GS score.

    Mains answer writing

    • GS I to III have 20 questions each: ten of 10 marks (about 150 words) and ten of 15 marks (about 250 words), in 3 hours.
    • Read the directive word first (discuss, examine, critically analyse) and answer exactly that.
    • Open with a definition or fact, give two or three dimensions in the body, close with a forward-looking line.
    • Use data, committees, cases and examples. One good example beats a paragraph of theory.
    • Write one answer daily, get it checked, and rewrite the weakest part. Practice with feedback is what moves marks.
    • Time yourself. Unfinished papers lose more marks than imperfect answers.

    Essay strategy

    • The paper has two sections with four topics each. You write one essay from each, 125 marks per essay.
    • Spend the first ten minutes choosing the topic and planning dimensions: social, economic, political, ethical, historical, global.
    • Keep one clear stand and a flow from introduction to conclusion, not a list of points.
    • Collect quotes, examples and data in a notebook through the year and revise it.
    • Practise full essays against the clock, and ask someone to evaluate them.

    Ethics (GS Paper IV) strategy

    • Learn core concepts in your own words: values, attitude, emotional intelligence, probity, ethics in governance.
    • Keep a short list of thinkers and one example for each concept.
    • For case studies, state the stakeholders, the dilemma, the options with pros and cons, and your course of action with reasons.
    • Stay practical and lawful. Examiners reward balanced, implementable decisions.
    • Write at least one case study a week.

    Basic information

    • The exam has three stages: Prelims, Mains and Interview.
    • You need a bachelor’s degree from a recognised university. Final-year students can apply and must show the degree at Mains.
    • General category age limit is 21 to 32. Relaxation: 3 years for OBC and 5 years for SC/ST, and more in some cases.
    • Attempts: 6 for General, 9 for OBC, and up to the age limit for SC/ST. Check the notification for other categories.
    • Exact dates, vacancies and rules are in the notification on upsc.gov.in. Always trust the notification over any other source.
